questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to win the lottery and spend the money wisely
Elon Musk's life and career as a technology tycoon
Bitcoin as an investment and the electricity it uses
Why Argentina uses so much electricity every year
questions.why: They discuss whether bitcoin is a good option for ordinary people and its impact on energy use.

questions.q: What did Elon Musk recently do, according to Sam?
options: He bought a lottery ticket and won a huge prize
He started his own cryptocurrency to compete with bitcoin
He criticised bitcoin publicly for its high energy use
He invested one and a half billion dollars in bitcoin
questions.why: Sam says he invested one and a half billion dollars in bitcoin.

questions.q: Why are green campaigners worried about bitcoin?
options: It makes ordinary people spend too much of their savings
Creating new bitcoins uses huge amounts of electricity
It is mostly used by criminals to hide their money
It is quickly replacing paper money and coins in shops
questions.why: Sam says mining bitcoins uses huge amounts of electricity, so campaigners question its impact.

questions.q: How much did Heather Delany invest in bitcoin at first?
options: About five dollars
About fifty dollars
The price of a lottery ticket
Her whole pension
questions.why: She says her initial investment was only around five dollars, the cost of a coffee and a pastry.

questions.q: How does Heather see her bitcoin now?
options: As a quick way to get rich in a few months
As a risky game she now regrets starting
As a long-term investment for her retirement
As extra money to spend on coffee and treats
questions.why: She sees it as a long-term investment and part of her overall pension plan.

questions.q: What does a recent estimate say about bitcoin's electricity use?
options: It is falling every year
It is now more than Argentina uses in a year
It is the same as one US city
It is less than a small village uses
questions.why: Rob says bitcoin has now overtaken the entire annual electricity use of Argentina.

questions.q: According to Michel Rauchs, what uses twice as much electricity as bitcoin?
options: All the computers in Cambridge University
The whole country of Argentina
Electric cars in Europe
US home appliances left on standby
questions.why: He says appliances on standby in the US use twice as much electricity as the bitcoin network each year.

questions.q: Why does Michel Rauchs make this comparison?
options: To show that bitcoin's energy use should be seen in context
To prove that bitcoin is completely harmless for the planet
To persuade more people to buy bitcoin while it is cheap
To criticise people who spend too many hours watching TV
questions.why: He says 'we need to put things a bit into perspective' before comparing.
